Mohyliv-Podilskyy New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This is the new Jewish cemetery of Mohyliv-Podilskyi, founded per the Commission on the Preservation of Jewish Heritage in the latter half of the 18th century. Jews are first documented in the town, then called Movilău after its Moldavian founding prince, around 1637; by the 1740s, Jews owned 170 houses, and in 1808 the father-and-son Shtein family relocated their Hebrew printing house to the town. The Jewish population reached 12,344 (more than 55 percent) by 1897, supported by 16 synagogues and prayer houses, six schools, a Talmud Torah, and a Jewish hospital by the early 20th century. Occupied by Romanian and German troops in July 1941 and absorbed into the Transnistria Governorate, the town became a major transit camp through which over 55,000 deportees passed between September 1941 and February 1942; in March 1944, Jewish leaders in Bucharest secured permission to bring back 1,400 orphans. This cemetery, next to the town's Christian one, holds around 5,000 graves.
